```markdown
# Breaking-change flag in release notes

Source: `specs/deferred_items.md`, item 7 (picked for Design via /deferred, 2026-11-10).

## Intent

`release-notes` writes one bullet per merged pull request. Breaking changes are
currently indistinguishable from any other bullet. We want each bullet to carry
a breaking flag so that:

- `announce` can put breaking changes first in its post, and
- people reading the notes can spot breaking changes at a glance.

`changelog-check` and `announce` both parse `release-notes` output, so they must
accept the new form.

## Goals

- A bullet for a breaking pull request is visibly marked in the notes.
- `parse.py` (`skills/changelog-check/parse.py`) recognises the mark and exposes
  it as `breaking=True` on the parsed entry. Unmarked entries get `breaking=False`.
- `announce` lists breaking entries before all others.

## Non-goals

- No change to how non-breaking bullets look or parse.
- No other new fields on bullets.
- No change to how pull requests get labelled; the `breaking` label is applied
  by people, as today.

## Anti-goals

- Older release notes (no tags) failing `changelog-check`, or parsing to
  anything different from today. That would make this a failure even if the
  new tag works.

## Constraints

- `parse.py` today splits each bullet on " — " and rejects a bullet with more
  than two parts. That rule stays as it is.

## Approaches

1. **Third part:** append " — breaking: yes" to the bullet and teach `parse.py`
   to accept three parts. Changes the split rule, and the flag sits at the end
   of the line where readers are least likely to see it.
2. **Leading tag (picked):** start the bullet with `[breaking]`, which
   `parse.py` strips before it splits. Untagged bullets parse exactly as
   before, so older notes stay valid, and the tag is the first thing a reader
   sees.

The partner picked 2, because existing notes stay valid unchanged.

## Design (decided with the partner)

- **`release-notes`** (`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`): when a merged pull
  request carries the `breaking` label, its bullet text starts with
  `[breaking] `. Otherwise the bullet is unchanged.
- **`parse.py`**: before splitting on " — ", strip a leading `[breaking]` from
  the bullet text and set `breaking=True` on the entry; otherwise
  `breaking=False`. The two-part rule then applies to the remainder as today.
- **`announce`** (`skills/announce/SKILL.md`): lists breaking entries first.
- **Test** in `skills/changelog-check/`: one tagged bullet (parses, `breaking`
  is True, the rest of the entry matches the untagged parse) and one untagged
  bullet (parses as today, `breaking` is False).

## Calls made by the designer (check these)

- The tag goes after the list marker and is followed by one space:
  `- [breaking] <rest of bullet>`.
- The tag is matched exactly, lowercase, only at the start of the bullet text.
  `[breaking]` anywhere else is ordinary text.
- `announce` keeps the original order within the breaking group and within the
  non-breaking group; it only moves breaking entries to the front.

## Left to the builder

- Whether `announce` reuses `parse.py` or its own reading of the bullets; either
  way it must honour the tag as above.
- How `announce` visually sets the breaking group apart in its post, if at all,
  beyond ordering.
- Test file name and structure, following what's already in
  `skills/changelog-check/`.
```
